patterns.title: Multiple Failed Logins from Single IP
patterns.description: An IP address making multiple failed login attempts within a short time period - possible brute force attack.

patterns.title: Same-Day In-Out Fund Movement
patterns.description: Account receiving funds and transferring them out on the same day - possible mule account or layering.

patterns.title: Odd-Hour Call Activity
patterns.description: Calls made between 11PM-5AM - possible coordinated activity or evasion.

patterns.title: Multiple IMEI Swaps
patterns.description: Number used with multiple IMEIs - possible handset swap or SIM swapping.

patterns.title: Funnel Account Pattern
patterns.description: Account receiving from many distinct senders and concentrating to few destinations - possible mule funnel.

patterns.title: Round-Figure Transactions
patterns.description: Multiple transactions with round amounts - possible structuring or layering.

patterns.title: High Pass-Through Ratio
patterns.description: Account passing through most of received funds - classic mule account signature.

patterns.title: Closed-Loop Pair
patterns.description: Two accounts only transacting with each other - possible coordinated operation.

patterns.title: Burner phone pattern
patterns.description: A large number of very short duration calls (under 10 seconds) to many different numbers over a short time window.

patterns.title: Mule account layering
patterns.description: Funds arrive from multiple senders into one account and are moved out within minutes/hours to another account, often just before the account is abandoned.

patterns.title: Odd-hour coordination
patterns.description: Repeated calls or transactions clustered between 11 PM and 5 AM, outside the subject's normal activity pattern.

patterns.title: Rapid IMEI change
patterns.description: A subscriber number switches to a completely different IMEI within a short period, suggesting SIM swapping or handset change to evade tracking.

patterns.title: Frequent small cash-outs
patterns.description: Consistently withdrawing or transferring funds in small amounts just below reporting thresholds - possible structuring.
